units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
A spacious garden-room, with one door to the left, and two doors to the right.
In the middle of the room a round table, with chairs about it.
On the table lie books, periodicals, and newspapers.
In the foreground to the left a window, and by it a small sofa, with a worktable in front of it.
In the background, the room is continued into a somewhat narrower conservatory, the walls of which are formed by large panes of glass.
In the right-hand wall of the conservatory is a door leading down into the garden.
Through the glass wall a gloomy fjord landscape is faintly visible, veiled by steady rain.
ENGSTRAND, the carpenter, stands by the garden door.
His left leg is somewhat bent; he has a clump of wood under the sole of his boot.
REGINA, with an empty garden syringe in her hand, hinders him from advancing.
In a low voice.
What do you want? Stop where you are. You're positively dripping.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: It's the Lord's own rain, my girl.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: It's the devil's rain, I say.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Lord, how you talk, Regina.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Limps a step or two forward into the room.
It's just this as I wanted to say--
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Don't clatter so with that foot of yours, I tell you! The young master's asleep upstairs.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Asleep? In the middle of the day?
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: It's no business of yours.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: I was out on the loose last night--
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: I can quite believe that.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Yes, we're weak vessels, we poor mortals, my girl--
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: So it seems.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: --and temptations are manifold in this world, you see. But all the same, I was hard at work, God knows, at half-past five this morning.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Very well; only be off now. I won't stop here and have rendezvous's
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Note: This and other French words by Regina are in that language in the original.
with you.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: What do you say you won't have?
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: I won't have any one find you here; so just you go about your business.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Advances a step or two.
Blest if I go before I've had a talk with you. This afternoon I shall have finished my work at the school house, and then I shall take to-night's boat and be off home to the town.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Mutters.
Pleasant journey to you!
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Thank you, my child. To-morrow the Orphanage is to be opened, and then there'll be fine doings, no doubt, and plenty of intoxicating drink going, you know. And nobody shall say of Jacob Engstrand that he can't keep out of temptation's way.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Oh!
units.name: REGINA

units.text: You see, there's to be heaps of grand folks here to-morrow. Pastor Manders is expected from town, too.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: He's coming to-day.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: There, you see! And I should be cursedly sorry if he found out anything against me, don't you understand?
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Oho! is that your game?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Is what my game?
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Looking hard at him.
What are you going to fool Pastor Manders into doing, this time?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Sh! sh! Are you crazy? Do I want to fool Pastor Manders? Oh no! Pastor Manders has been far too good a friend to me for that. But I just wanted to say, you know--that I mean to be off home again to-night.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: The sooner the better, say I.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Yes, but I want you with me, Regina.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Open-mouthed.
You want me--? What are you talking about?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: I want you to come home with me, I say.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Scornfully.
Never in this world shall you get me home with you.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Oh, we'll see about that.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Yes, you may be sure we'll see about it! Me, that have been brought up by a lady like Mrs. Alving! Me, that am treated almost as a daughter here! Is it me you want to go home with you?--to a house like yours? For shame!
units.name: REGINA
